candidates.title: Retraction: Procrastination, Deadlines, and Performance: Self-Control by Precommitment
candidates.review_notes: The publisher now labels the 2002 Ariely-Wertenbroch paper retracted. Brali should not cite the original paper as positive evidence for deadline design.

candidates.title: Evidence of impact and interpretational limits of generative AI in STEM education: a systematic review and meta-analysis on cognitive learning outcomes
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access peer-reviewed article and its detailed methods/results material were reviewed. The systematic review found 85 eligible controlled quantitative STEM-learning studies; 49 studies contributed 59 effect sizes to the meta-analysis. A conventional random-effects model appeared positive, but heterogeneity was extreme (I²=96.32%), the prediction interval included negative through strongly positive effects, funnel asymmetry suggested publication bias, and a robust Bayesian publication-bias correction favored the absence of a stable overall positive or negative effect. Moderator analyses were more informative: learning outcome type and the degree to which AI augmented versus substituted learners' cognitive activity explained some heterogeneity, with the authors concluding that AI appears more promising when it augments learner activity rather than replacing it. The review also found that many apparently large effects came from intervention and control groups doing cognitively incomparable work, and all included studies were rated high risk of bias. This supports Brali's existing human-first AI collaboration boundary in learning contexts, not a blanket claim that AI improves learning or that one prompt/workflow is optimal.

candidates.title: Effects of exercise snacks on cardiorespiratory fitness, body composition, and blood lipids in adults across different age groups: a systematic review and meta-analysis
candidates.container_title: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed, not just discovery metadata. The review searched six databases through April 15, 2026, included 21 randomized controlled studies with 921 adults, and synthesized exercise-snack interventions including stair climbing, resistance exercise, cycling and sprint-interval exercise. Pooled effects favored VO2max (Hedges g 1.04, 95% CI 0.68–1.39; I2 74%) and peak power output (g 0.68, 95% CI 0.25–1.10; I2 63%), both graded moderate certainty. Body-fat and lipid outcomes were low certainty or inconclusive. Study-level subgroup patterns suggested differences by daily bout count, weekly frequency and intervention length, but these observational comparisons across small numbers of studies should not be treated as an optimal prescription.

candidates.title: The effects of progressive muscle relaxation on sleep quality in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access publisher article reviewed, not just discovery metadata. The review searched CINAHL, Embase, PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science through May 2026 and included 14 randomized controlled trials with 957 participants. All included populations had cancer or other clinical/chronic conditions; the review did not establish the same effect in a general healthy population. The pooled result favored PMR for subjective PSQI sleep quality (Hedges g -1.24, 95% CI -1.71 to -0.77), but heterogeneity was very high (I2 85.5%). Egger's test suggested possible publication bias (p=0.004); trim-and-fill reduced the estimate to g -0.92 while retaining the same direction. Intervention duration ranged from 3 days to 12 weeks and session counts varied widely. Meta-regression did not find a statistically significant association between session count and effect size (p=0.2106), which does not establish an optimal cadence. The age >=55 subgroup was imprecise, and the formal test for difference between age groups was not significant, so the review does not support a claim that PMR stops working after age 55.

candidates.title: Replication of Procrastination, Deadlines, and Performance: Self-Control by Precommitment
candidates.review_notes: The 2026 replication of Study 2 from Ariely and Wertenbroch did not reproduce the original deadline effect: deadline changes had negligible effects on reported performance and survey metrics. This directly challenges treating artificial deadlines as a settled productivity hack.

candidates.title: Mixed effects of retrieval practice on the acquisition of procedural knowledge in verb spelling education
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision retrieval-procedural-application-2026 challenges the assumption that better rule retention means better application. In this classroom study, retrieval plus worked examples improved rule retention after one week but not rule application compared with worked examples alone.

candidates.title: Exercise Snacks Are Feasible to Perform in the Real World and Improve Physical Capacity for Adults Living With Non-Insulin Treated Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomised Trial
candidates.review_notes: Published randomized trial checked against the full available manuscript and published record. Sixty-nine insufficiently active adults with non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes (mean age 58 years; 46 female) were randomized for 12 weeks to four 1-minute vigorous exercise snacks or four 1-minute low-intensity mobility/stretching bouts on at least five days per week. Weekly adherence was about 18 bouts in both groups. The vigorous group worked harder and improved 30-second sit-to-stand performance by 1.9 repetitions more than the active comparator, but there were no between-group differences for the other reported secondary outcomes, including HbA1c, cardiometabolic blood biomarkers, estimated VO2max, grip strength and anthropometrics.

candidates.title: Examining the relationship between supervisory feedback characteristics and employee feedback processing: a systematic review and meta-analysis
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access Current Psychology article reviewed. The synthesis covered 24 peer-reviewed studies, 595,950 participants, 75 effect sizes and 26 supervisory-feedback characteristics. Credibility and feedback quality were among the more consistent correlates of how employees perceived, accepted and intended to respond to feedback. However, most included studies were correlational and self-report, heterogeneity was very high (I²=95%), and context variables such as channel and feedback frequency were inconsistently reported. Brali should treat source credibility and clear/specific/constructive feedback as design hypotheses to test, not as experimentally established causal components or a basis for promising performance improvement.

candidates.title: A Self-Guided Mobile Mindfulness Intervention Embedded in Daily Routines for Adults With Mild to Moderate Psychological Distress: Randomized Controlled Trial
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed via PubMed Central, not just title/abstract metadata. The four-arm parallel RCT randomized 686 adults aged 18-65 with mild to moderate anxiety or depressive symptoms in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to Traditional Mindfulness (TM), Habitual Mindfulness Practice (HMP), Mindfulness-Based Psychoeducation (MBP), or waitlist. The 21-day HMP program embedded three audio-guided five-minute practices per day into recurring daily contexts; TM used one continuous 15-minute daily practice. HMP and TM had lower postintervention depressive and anxiety symptom scores than MBP and waitlist, although TM had lower postintervention anxiety than HMP. The key implementation result for Brali is negative as well as positive: HMP did not differ significantly from TM in total practice duration, self-reported engagement, participant satisfaction, or attrition. Attrition was substantial. Postintervention outcome data were available for 55.2% (379/686) of randomized participants; three-month outcome data were available for 24.1% (124/515) of participants assigned to active conditions. The study used self-report outcomes and app-derived engagement measures. It did not directly measure habit strength, automaticity, or cue-response consistency. The authors therefore could not establish habit formation as the mechanism. The intervention was a multi-component mobile program totaling 15 minutes per day, not a trial of Brali's simple five-minute breath practice.

candidates.title: Acute cognitive effects of interruptions to prolonged sitting with brief standing or physical activity breaks: a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis
candidates.container_title: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision movement-breaks-cognition-2026 reviewed the source and keeps this as watch: the meta-analysis reports small acute executive/memory effects but mostly low or very-low certainty and does not justify a cognitive-optimization break interval, duration, or intensity prescription.

candidates.title: A cross-over feasibility trial of smartphone grayscale mode in medical students
candidates.review_notes: Complete open-access Frontiers article reviewed. Sixty-one first-year medical students enrolled and 51 completed both consecutive one-week conditions. Assignment used an alternating sequence based on enrollment order, followed by cross-over between grayscale and normal color. Participants reported the screen-time values shown by built-in phone tracking. Mixed-effects analyses found about 28 minutes/day lower mean screen time under grayscale. Exploratory non-validated productivity and sleep items did not show consistent significant differences. The trial was short, unblinded, had no washout, relied on participant transcription of device screen-time values, and qualitative responses described usability problems and substitution to other devices.

candidates.title: Research on the testing effect routinely conflates direct and forward testing effects: A meta-analysis of testing effects with free recall
candidates.container_title: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision testing-effect-direct-forward-2026 challenges undifferentiated testing-effect language. The meta-analysis separates direct memory benefits for tested material from forward effects on subsequently learned material and finds that most included effects came from mixed designs.

candidates.title: Using behavioral science to improve compliance in government records management: Evidence from a large field experiment
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access Government Information Quarterly article reviewed. In a pre-registered field experiment with 22,774 employees across 35 agencies in a Canadian provincial government, the intervention combined an initial message, an opt-in recurring 10-minute weekly calendar appointment for two months, and a new expert-approved records-management tip each week. Relative to status quo control, both motivational framings reduced network-drive storage by about 5%, with no credible difference between personal-benefit and injunctive-norm framing; a similar decrease appeared when the control group later received the intervention. Storage volume was an objective administrative outcome but only a proxy for file-level compliance, and the multi-component treatment cannot identify which component caused the effect. Brali should therefore test a bounded recurring maintenance block only where retention and archival rules are known, without treating ten minutes weekly as an optimal dose or encouraging indiscriminate deletion.

candidates.title: Digital disconnection as a self-regulatory strategy against procrastination
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. A preregistered two-week experience-sampling study followed 237 young adult Android users across 12,408 observations. Within a person, moments with deliberate digital disconnection were associated with slightly less procrastination, and exploratory lagged analyses showed a small association into the following measurement window. Device-, application- and feature-level disconnection showed the most promising pattern. The study is observational, self-reported and limited to young adults; reverse causality and time-varying confounding remain possible. It supports the situational design of a phone-offline protocol but does not establish causal effectiveness.

candidates.title: The impact of walking on creative thinking: A systematic review and meta-analysis
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed. Twenty-three studies (1,036 participants) found moderate-certainty evidence that walking improves divergent thinking; randomized-only sensitivity analysis remained positive. Evidence for convergent thinking was very uncertain and did not show a clear benefit. Heterogeneity was substantial and most samples were post-secondary students.

candidates.title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Facilitate Difficult Conversations
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. In a preregistered randomized two-part study, 1,465 US/Canadian Prolific participants completed the initial session and 1,371 returned for follow-up. Participants who spent 6-12 minutes preparing a real difficult conversation with a GPT-4o-mini chatbot were more likely to report having that conversation over the following week than participants who used the same chatbot for neutral factual questions (65% vs 59%). The study supports preparation as an initiation aid, not a claim that AI improves the eventual conversation: among participants who did have the conversation, satisfaction, perceived quality, difficulty and thoroughness did not significantly differ. Brali should propose a bounded rehearsal workflow for ordinary, safe conversations that the person already judges worth having, with explicit exclusions for abuse, coercion, legal/HR-sensitive disputes and situations requiring professional support or documentation.

candidates.title: The Acute Effects of Interrupting Prolonged Sitting With Regular Activity Breaks on Postprandial Glucose and Insulin in Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. The review identified 53 acute laboratory randomized crossover studies and included 39 in meta-analysis. Regular activity breaks during prolonged sitting reduced postprandial glucose and insulin iAUC versus uninterrupted sitting; walking produced the strongest overall mode estimates, and more frequent break subgroups showed larger acute effects. The evidence is causal for short-term metabolic responses but not for long-term disease outcomes. Heterogeneity was often high, most studies were only fair or good on the modified risk-of-bias tool, prolonged-sitting laboratory protocols may not reflect ordinary life, and the review itself was not prospectively registered and had no prepared protocol. Brali should therefore propose a flexible 'break up prolonged sitting with brief movement' protocol rather than canonizing one universal 20-minute interval.

candidates.title: Bias in the Loop: How Humans Evaluate AI-Generated Suggestions
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. In a factorial experiment with 2,784 U.S. Prolific annotators verifying AI-extracted greenhouse-gas values, making rejection of an AI suggestion more laborious by requiring the reviewer to type the corrected value reduced correction activity and increased undercorrection. The overall accuracy effect was not robustly negative because overcorrections also fell. Pre-existing favorable attitudes toward AI were associated with more undercorrection and lower accuracy, but that association was not randomized. The study used crowdworkers, one annotation domain, ten reports, and several difficult items requiring domain knowledge, so it does not establish a universal effect size or a general rule that skepticism improves judgment.

candidates.title: Spoken disagreement is more constructive than written disagreement
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. Across randomized disagreement experiments, speaking produced greater perceived understanding and generally lower perceived conflict than writing. Samples were mostly students or strangers, conflict was relatively low, and the paper does not establish the same effect for close relationships, workplace disputes, unsafe situations, or settings where a written record matters.

candidates.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis on the effectiveness of if-then plans – in a strict sense – to facilitate fruit and vegetable consumption in adults
candidates.container_title: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis reviewed. Ten peer-reviewed randomized controlled trial reports provided 12 active-control comparisons with 2,399 adults and follow-up periods from 1 week to 24 months. The review deliberately excluded vague action-planning procedures and retained interventions that explicitly linked a perceivable situation to a goal-directed response. Compared with similarly motivated active controls, if-then planning produced a small average increase in self-reported fruit-and-vegetable intake (MD 0.29 portions/day, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.48; SMD about 0.20; I² 32%). All intake outcomes were retrospective self-report, samples were predominantly young-to-middle-aged Western European, female and Caucasian, and the review did not prospectively register a public protocol. Brali should therefore offer the method as a low-cost planning experiment for an existing intention to eat more fruit or vegetables, not as medical nutrition advice, an optimal diet, or evidence of clinical health benefit.

candidates.title: Effects of green exercise on mental health: a systematic review and meta-analysis
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access publisher article reviewed, not just discovery metadata. The PROSPERO-registered review searched five databases through 7 November 2025 and included 51 peer-reviewed RCTs or crossover RCTs with 3,092 healthy adults aged 18-85. Most interventions were walking (72.5%); the authors state the findings primarily reflect low-intensity walking in natural environments. Green exercise improved overall wellbeing and affect across pooled comparisons with non-exercise, indoor exercise and built-up outdoor exercise. Stress-specific pooled effects favored green exercise versus non-exercise (SMD -0.51, 95% CI -0.81 to -0.20; I2 0%; 3 studies), indoor exercise (SMD -0.34, 95% CI -0.56 to -0.11; I2 53.5%; 6 studies) and built-up exercise (SMD -0.38, 95% CI -0.67 to -0.09; I2 0%; 2 studies). Several other outcomes had high heterogeneity. Most interventions were short-term with follow-up generally under three months; many individual studies were small and had limitations in randomization reporting/blinding. The review does not establish an optimal duration, a required type of green space, a unique mechanism, or durable long-term effects.

candidates.title: Promoting Self-Regulated Social Media Use on Smartphones With a Mobile Intervention App (Wellspent): Randomized Controlled Trial
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. In a preregistered 3-week randomized trial, 70 adult iPhone users who regularly used social media were randomized 1:1 to a customizable digital self-control app or no-treatment control. The intervention bundled user-selected target apps, daily limits, self-defined continuous-use nudge intervals, customizable full-screen reminders, alternative activities, feedback and self-monitoring; reminders required an active quit-or-continue decision but did not block access. The intervention group reduced objectively recorded time on its self-identified most problematic social-media app by about 29 minutes per day relative to control, while problematic social-media use and self-efficacy did not improve robustly. The final primary-outcome model included 46 participants, follow-up was short, 26% did not complete week 3, only iPhone users were studied, and two authors had ties to Wellspent GmbH. Because multiple intervention components were delivered together, Brali must not attribute the effect to the full-screen checkpoint alone. The evidence supports testing a bounded, user-configured social-media brake as a package, not claiming treatment, improved wellbeing, or a universal time limit.

candidates.title: Optimizing physical activity bouts to interrupt sedentary behaviour for cardiometabolic health: a systematic review and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials
candidates.review_notes: Full Oxford Academic article reviewed. The review synthesized 144 randomized studies, 247 intervention arms, and 2,216 adults in acute controlled settings. Physical-activity interruptions produced favourable average acute effects on glucose and insulin; the review rated pooled glucose and insulin evidence high certainty with GRADE. More frequent light-to-moderate bouts were favourable for glucose. Standing-only interventions did not show the same acute cardiometabolic signal. The authors emphasize heterogeneous protocols, many small samples, and the gap between acute laboratory responses and sustainable long-term clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Relying on AI at work reduces self-efficacy, ownership, and meaning while active collaboration mitigates the effects
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. In a preregistered experiment (N=269), directly copying AI-generated work reduced psychological ownership and meaningfulness relative to both no-AI and a human-first/AI-refinement workflow; AI-independent self-efficacy was also lower than no-AI. A follow-up survey (N=270) showed directionally consistent associations across broader work tasks but was correlational. The causal task was occupation-specific writing and the passive condition was deliberately extreme, so the source does not establish one optimal AI workflow for all work.

candidates.title: Effectiveness of savoring interventions: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
candidates.review_notes: Complete open-access meta-analysis reviewed. Twenty independent randomized trials with 4,805 adult participants contributed 45 effects. A three-level random-effects model estimated a moderate overall pooled effect on emotional outcomes (g 0.51, 95% CI 0.26 to 0.77), but total heterogeneity was high (I2 86.61%). Twelve studies used active controls and eight passive controls; active-control point estimates were smaller although control type did not reach statistical significance as a moderator. Thirty percent of studies were high risk of bias, most outcomes were self-reported, intervention formats varied, median duration was 14 days, and the review did not establish one concrete savoring micro-practice or long-term effect.

candidates.title: Duolingo-inspired pretesting with words and pictures improves vocabulary learning
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. Across four preregistered experiments with adult online learners, multiple-choice guessing followed by correct-answer feedback before study improved short-delay cued recall of Spanish word-image and image-word pairs versus reading-only study; benefits were modest and multiple-choice benefits were less consistent. The experiments used concrete nouns, Prolific samples, a five-minute distractor before the criterial test, and pretesting trials gave learners extra cue-only exposure before feedback. The protocol proposal is therefore narrow: guess before reveal for new concrete L2 vocabulary, then show the correct answer immediately and later test recall. It does not support long-term retention, grammar, conversation, general learning, or the claim that errors themselves are beneficial. Pretesting is kept distinct from retrieval practice because the target has not yet been learned.

candidates.title: Wakeful rest and memory consolidation in an ecologically valid educational setting: no benefit over distractor tasks
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. In a randomized classroom study, 161 university students read an expository text and were assigned to eight minutes of wakeful rest, social media, math problems, or a content-similar reading task. Immediate and one-week tests measured factual recall and conceptual understanding. Wakeful rest did not show a consistent advantage over the distractor conditions. This is an important boundary for Brali: the existing meta-analytic support for wakeful rest concerns declarative-memory paradigms and should not be presented as proof that quiet rest improves comprehension or retention of complex educational material.

candidates.title: Micro-exercise breaks every hour: a feasible strategy to improve metabolic health in sedentary office workers
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. Eighty-six sedentary Chinese office workers aged 25-55 were randomized to 12 weeks of seven 3-minute equipment-free micro-exercise breaks across an 8-hour workday or usual behavior. The intervention improved several objectively measured metabolic outcomes and reduced accelerometer-measured sedentary time; 79 participants completed follow-up and mean reported adherence was 82%. This is useful longer-duration workplace evidence, but it remains a single small trial in one city with a predominantly overweight sample. It was not registered in a clinical-trial registry, had no attention control, relied largely on self-reported adherence, did not monitor diet, and cannot establish disease prevention or an optimal hourly 3-minute dose. Keep it on watch as ecological support rather than using it to hard-code the protocol.

candidates.title: Beyond positive thinking: A randomized trial of mental contrasting with implementation intentions to curb academic procrastination
candidates.review_notes: Source review completed for the WOOP/MCII Gold boundary. The study randomized 101 eligible first-year undergraduates at one private Chinese university; 20 were excluded during the seven-day period for missing reports or failure to follow the assigned intervention, leaving 81 participants in the final sample (41 MCII, 40 positive-thinking control; 19.8% attrition). Outcomes were primarily self-report, with diary-based task initiation used as behavioral verification, and the follow-up horizon was one week. Retain as narrow support for obstacle-plus-plan task initiation in this context only; do not generalize to universal anti-procrastination, long-term goal achievement, workplaces, clinical populations, or treatment.

candidates.title: A systematic review of technology-mediated conflict management in couples
candidates.container_title: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access systematic review reviewed. Fifteen quantitative studies directly compared technology-mediated and face-to-face couple conflict. The overall pattern was mixed and did not support one universally superior mode; potential moderators included attachment, self-esteem and relationship satisfaction. The evidence base is early and heterogeneous, includes seven grey-literature studies, many small experimental samples, mostly satisfied low-conflict couples, and technologies spanning 2007-2024. This source is a direct boundary against generalizing a spoken-over-written disagreement finding to romantic conflict as a universal rule.

candidates.title: Reducing Work-Related Screen-Time in Healthcare Workers During Leisure Time (REDUCE SCREEN) – A Randomized Controlled Trial
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access Journal of Medical Systems article reviewed. In a preregistered pragmatic parallel RCT, 815 US healthcare workers with a work-email app on their smartphone were randomized before an off-work weekend to usual behavior or a three-part intervention encouraging an automatic out-of-office reply, lower leisure screen time, and removal of work apps from personal devices. Among 520 participants with post-weekend outcome data, baseline-adjusted perceived stress was 1.6 PSS-10 points lower in the intervention group (95% CI -2.6 to -0.6), and the intervention group had higher odds of lower screen time. The randomized treatment tested the package, not any component in isolation; the apparent advantage among participants who uninstalled work apps was exploratory and self-selected. Brali can therefore propose a bounded 'protect off-work time from work apps' experiment for genuinely off-duty periods, while preserving emergency/on-call access and avoiding a claim that uninstalling an app is itself the proven active ingredient.

candidates.title: The association between sleep variability and cognitive function: A systematic review and meta analysis
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision sleep-variability-cognition-2026 reviewed the publisher source and keeps this as watch: greater sleep variability is associated with poorer cognition on average, but the evidence does not justify a causal sleep-regularity protocol or fixed schedule prescription.

candidates.title: Should we all just take 10? A meta-analysis of wakeful rest
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision wakeful-rest-memory-2026 supports a conservative post-learning quiet-rest experiment. The source reports substantial heterogeneity and weaker effects in healthy young to middle-aged adults, so Brali does not publish a universal ten-minute dose or guaranteed memory benefit.

candidates.title: The leisure crafting intervention: Effects on work and non-work outcomes and the moderating role of age
candidates.review_notes: Full Human Relations article reviewed. A five-week randomized online intervention among 462 Dutch employees paired a brief explanation of leisure crafting with a self-development plan built around an existing or new leisure activity and weekly reflection. The plan explicitly combined autonomous goal-setting, learning and human connection. Relative to a passive control, the intervention produced greater growth in self-reported meaning at work and employee creativity, but not work engagement or the general non-work outcomes that were tested. Affective well-being improved only in the older region of the sample. The evidence supports a bounded personal experiment in deliberately structuring one leisure activity for autonomy, learning and connection, then reviewing spillover; it does not support claims about job performance, universal well-being, an optimal hobby, or a fixed dose.

candidates.title: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of well-being-focused interventions
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access Nature Human Behaviour article reviewed. The preregistered network meta-analysis included 183 randomized controlled trials and 22,811 adults without diagnosed conditions. Mindfulness, compassion, yoga, exercise and single positive-psychology interventions generally improved well-being versus inactive controls, with no consistent evidence that the better-supported approaches clearly outperformed one another. Mindfulness had the broadest direct evidence base among the contemplative approaches. The review also reports major quality constraints: 60% of included trials were rated high risk of bias, only 33% used intention-to-treat analysis, funnel-plot asymmetry suggested publication bias, many outcomes were immediate post-intervention, and many network comparisons were indirect. Brali should therefore use this source to support choice among several bounded wellbeing practices, not to crown a universal best technique or prescribe a fixed dose.

candidates.title: The Effect of Prequestions on Learning: A Multilevel Meta-Analysis
candidates.review_notes: Multilevel meta-analysis reports a clear benefit for information targeted by prequestions (g = 0.66) and essentially no general benefit for non-prequestioned information (g = 0.01). Conditions combining feedback with prequestions showed stronger targeted learning than prequestions alone. Publish only as a targeting protocol: ask specific questions, attempt an answer, learn, and check. Do not claim broad lesson-wide improvement, a magic question count, or guaranteed benefit for every learner.

candidates.title: Give Me a Choice! A Field Experiment on Task Choice Enabled by Wearables
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. The study compared digitally delegated troubleshooting tasks with a choice-based smartwatch interface across two comparable manufacturing plants, using a plant-level randomized allocation plus Difference-in-Differences analysis of 31,429 tasks and 66,233 machine status reports. Choice increased response time by about 80 seconds, decreased accepted-task completion time by about 26 seconds, and did not significantly change aggregate machine productivity. The authors therefore recommend treating choice as context-dependent and considering hybrid assignment. Because there were only two plants in one company, the post-treatment period was short, skills could not be perfectly matched, and the tasks were brief breakdown-response work, Brali should not generalize this into a broad autonomy rule for knowledge work. Keep it on watch while using the finding to drive a new research lens: choice may be useful when response latency is cheap, while urgent tasks may need direct ownership.

candidates.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of educational approaches to reduce cognitive biases among students
candidates.review_notes: Full author-provided article and publisher record reviewed. The systematic review identified 54 randomized controlled trials with 383 effect sizes and 10,941 participants; the main meta-analysis of 160 effects from 41 studies found a small average reduction in targeted biases (g 0.26, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.39). Many interventions used cognitive strategies including consider-the-opposite and feedback. All included studies had unclear or high risk of bias, some publication-bias risk was present, and the authors explicitly highlight uncertainty about depth and transfer beyond trained tasks. The review supports modest expectations for debiasing training and argues against broad real-world claims.

candidates.title: Voice AI in Firms: A Natural Field Experiment on Automated Job Interviews
candidates.review_notes: Full 2026 working-paper version reviewed through the authors' public arXiv HTML. In a preregistered natural field experiment, 67,056 eligible applications were randomized across AI interviewer, human interviewer, and choice conditions within a high-volume recruitment firm in the Philippines. Human recruiters retained all final hiring decisions. AI-led interviews increased job offers and downstream job starts/retention without a measured productivity decline among hires. Transcript analyses show greater structure and consistency in AI interviews, but the proposed controlled-variance mechanism is not itself isolated by randomization. Five percent of AI interviews ended because applicants did not want to speak to AI and seven percent encountered technical failures. The evidence is a working paper and a single high-volume entry-level hiring context, not a general license to automate consequential judgment.

candidates.title: Enhancing the Peer-Feedback Process Through Instructional Support: A Meta-Analysis
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access meta-analysis reviewed. Across 32 journal studies with 3,806 learners, peer-feedback with instructional support outperformed unsupported peer-feedback overall (g=0.47). Support aimed at the feedback provider showed medium positive effects on feedback-provision quality, while evidence for support aimed specifically at feedback reception was too sparse to support a stable conclusion. The authors could not isolate one best fine-grained tool because rubrics, sentence starters, guiding questions, preparatory activities and integrated supports appeared in too few studies individually. This is useful support for Brali's existing educational peer-writing workflow: make the requested review target explicit and give the reviewer a small structure rather than asking for vague general feedback. It does not justify a universal rubric, professional-writing transfer, or a claim that structured peer feedback increases subject-matter knowledge.

candidates.title: Dose and timing effects of caffeine on subsequent sleep: a randomized clinical crossover trial
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. In a placebo-controlled, double-blind randomized crossover trial, 23 healthy men aged 18–40 with moderate habitual caffeine intake completed placebo and 100 mg or 400 mg caffeine conditions at 12, 8, or 4 hours before habitual bedtime. Objective sleep was measured with in-home partial polysomnography and subjective sleep with diaries. A 400 mg single dose disrupted several sleep outcomes, with effects detectable even when consumed 12 hours before bed and generally larger closer to bedtime. No statistically significant objective or subjective sleep effects were detected for 100 mg at the tested timings. The small all-male sample, acute capsule dosing, and narrow population mean Brali should not turn the null 100 mg result into a universal four-hour safety rule or the 400 mg result into a universal cutoff for every caffeine dose.

candidates.title: Enhancing Academic Performance Through Self-Explanation in Digital Learning Environments (DLEs): A Three-Level Meta-Analysis
candidates.review_notes: Three-level meta-analysis of 204 effect sizes from 56 studies in digital learning environments reports an overall positive effect on academic performance (g = 0.46), with positive retention and transfer effects and moderation by pacing and knowledge type. Publish a bounded generate-check-correct protocol. Do not claim one best modality, prompt, frequency, or universal effect outside the reviewed digital-learning context.

candidates.title: Blocking mobile internet on smartphones improves sustained attention, mental health, and subjective well-being
candidates.review_notes: Full open-access article reviewed. In a preregistered month-long randomized delayed-intervention trial, participants assigned to block all mobile internet on their smartphones for two weeks improved on an objectively measured sustained-attention task, alongside self-reported wellbeing outcomes. Calls, texts and internet on other devices remained available. Adherence was difficult: only 119 of 467 people who agreed to the intervention met the preregistered compliance threshold. The sample was unusually motivated to reduce smartphone use, attrition was substantial, and expectancy effects could affect self-reports. Brali should therefore use the source to justify a bounded attention experiment, not a mental-health treatment claim, a universal screen-time limit, or a requirement to block mobile internet for two full weeks.

candidates.title: How effective is feedback for L1, L2, and FL learners’ writing? A meta-analysis
candidates.review_notes: Evidence Decision writing-feedback-level-match-2024 supports a narrow educational-writing protocol that distinguishes surface and deep revision targets. The source does not justify a universal feedback source, sequence, cadence, or transfer claim outside the secondary-school and university writing contexts reviewed.

candidates.title: The when and how of planning: Meta-analysis of the scope and components of implementation intentions in 642 tests
candidates.review_notes: Across 642 independent tests, implementation intentions produced positive cognitive, affective and behavioral effects; effects were larger for contingent if-then formats, when motivation was high, and when plans were rehearsed. Use as evidence for cue-response planning, not as a guaranteed effect size for every productivity task.

candidates.title: Effects of task interruptions caused by notifications from communication applications on strain and performance
candidates.review_notes: One-day field experiment, N=247. Disabling automatic communication notifications reduced notification interruptions; the reduction in interruptions was linked through significant indirect effects to higher self-reported performance and lower irritation. The direct intervention effect on performance was not significant and FoMO/telepressure mattered. Use as support for bounded notification-off focus windows, not an always-off prescription.

candidates.title: Effect of a Coaching Intervention to Improve Cardiologist Communication: A Randomized Clinical Trial
candidates.review_notes: The full randomized-trial report was reviewed. The intervention trained five behaviors together and used repeated individual coaching with feedback. It improved empathic statements, responses to empathic opportunities and question elicitation, but did not significantly increase reflective statements or open-ended questions; patient-reported communication effects could not be assessed because of ceiling effects. It therefore cannot validate Brali's paraphrase-plus-open-question protocol as an independently effective intervention.

candidates.title: After Dinner Rest a While, After Supper Walk a Mile? A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis on the Acute Postprandial Glycemic Response to Exercise Before and After Meal Ingestion in Healthy Subjects and Patients with Impaired Glucose Tolerance
candidates.review_notes: Complete open-access preregistered systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis reviewed. Eight randomized crossover trials with 30 interventions and 116 participants were included; 47 participants had type 2 diabetes and 69 did not. Exercise after eating reduced acute postprandial glucose excursions versus inactive control and performed better on average than matched pre-meal exercise. Shorter meal-to-exercise delay moderated the effect. The evidence base was small, included heterogeneous protocols, and the trials were rated high risk of bias. The review does not establish a universal walk duration, pace, exact start time, long-term disease prevention, or treatment guidance.

candidates.title: Give me a break! A systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of micro-breaks for increasing well-being and performance
candidates.review_notes: The full open-access article was reviewed, including eligibility criteria, risk-of-bias assessment, pooled well-being and performance results, moderator analyses and discussion. The review included 19 publications yielding 22 independent samples and 2,335 participants. Micro-breaks were defined as task interruptions of no more than 10 minutes. Small pooled improvements were reported for vigor and fatigue, while the pooled overall performance effect was not statistically significant. Only four of the 22 samples were rated low risk of bias, performance results were heterogeneous, and longer breaks were associated with better performance in meta-regression.

candidates.title: Behavioral interventions to extend sleep duration: A systematic review and meta-analysis
candidates.review_notes: Reviewed as support for a conservative sleep-opportunity protocol. The meta-analysis supports extending sleep duration through behavioral interventions but reports very high heterogeneity and does not identify an individual's ideal duration or prove a fixed regularity rule.

candidates.title: Experimental evidence that apologies promote forgiveness by communicating relationship value
candidates.review_notes: Reviewed as experimental support for apology as one possible interpersonal repair signal. It does not establish a universal apology script, guarantee forgiveness, restore trust automatically, or make apology appropriate in coercive or unsafe situations.

candidates.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Effects of Mental Contrasting With Implementation Intentions on Goal Attainment
candidates.review_notes: The full open-access meta-analysis was reviewed. It included 21 empirical articles contributing 24 independent effect sizes and 15,907 participants. The random-effects pooled effect was small-to-medium (Hedges' g=0.336, 95% CI 0.229 to 0.443) with medium heterogeneity (I2=59.321%). Publication-bias analyses were mixed; trim-and-fill produced a smaller adjusted estimate (0.242, 95% CI 0.143 to 0.342). The authors explicitly called for more studies on moderators.

candidates.title: Does time management work? A meta-analysis
candidates.review_notes: Meta-analysis of 158 studies / 53,957 participants found moderate relationships between time management and job performance, academic achievement and wellbeing, with substantial heterogeneity. Much of the evidence is correlational. It supports time-management as a broad construct, not any exact planner format, calendar ratio or time-block recipe.

candidates.title: Teaching temptation bundling to boost exercise: A field experiment
candidates.container_title: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
candidates.review_notes: Full open article reviewed. A large gym-based StepUp program tested free audiobooks with and without explicit temptation-bundling encouragement and also compared those groups with a no-audiobook control. The preregistered randomized comparison included 2,334 eligible gym members; a broader comparison included 6,792 members. Explicit teaching added only a modest incremental effect over receiving the audiobook alone, while audiobook-plus-encouragement versus control increased weekly workout likelihood and gym visits by roughly 10-14%/10-12% in reported analyses, with some effects persisting after the intervention. The evidence remains exercise-specific and bundled with other StepUp components such as planning, reminders and small rewards. The original university field experiment also found strong initial effects that decayed over time and after a holiday disruption.

candidates.title: Batching smartphone notifications can improve well-being
candidates.review_notes: Full article reviewed. In a two-week randomized field experiment, 237 participants recruited via MTurk used a custom smartphone notification system and were assigned to usual delivery, hourly batching, three daily batches, or no notifications. Three daily batches reduced perceived interruptions and stress and improved several self-reported outcomes relative to control; hourly batching produced little change, while the no-notification condition increased anxiety and FoMO. The study used one custom implementation, a short follow-up, an online-recruited sample, and a broad exploratory set of mostly subjective outcomes, so neither three batches nor the broader wellbeing effects should be treated as universal.

candidates.title: Targeting Procrastination Using Psychological Treatments: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
candidates.review_notes: The full article was reviewed, including eligibility criteria, included-study characteristics, pooled results, heterogeneity, risk of bias, discussion and conclusions. It supports a cautious statement that heterogeneous psychological treatments produced a small average post-treatment benefit on self-reported procrastination versus inactive controls. It does not isolate a five-minute start, one first action, a timer duration, implementation intentions, sub-goals or any other single component as the causal mechanism.

candidates.title: Tasks Interrupted: How Anticipating Time Pressure on Resumption of an Interrupted Task Causes Attention Residue and Low Performance on Interrupting Tasks and How a Ready-to-Resume Plan Mitigates the Effects
candidates.review_notes: Across four studies, anticipating a pressured return to unfinished work increased attention residue and reduced performance on the interrupting task; a brief ready-to-resume plan mitigated those effects. This supports a narrow pre-switch resumption note, not a universal productivity gain, fixed note length, or claim that all interruptions can be neutralized.

candidates.title: Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence
candidates.review_notes: Meta-analysis of 138 randomized studies (N=19,951). Interventions that increased monitoring of goal progress improved goal attainment on average (d+=0.40); effects were larger when progress was physically recorded or reported/made public. This supports visible progress tracking, but not one universal cadence, dashboard or streak system.

candidates.title: Checking email less frequently reduces stress
candidates.review_notes: Complete experimental report reviewed. In a two-week within-subject field study, 124 adults experienced one limited-email week and one unlimited-email week in randomized order. Participants were instructed to limit checking to three times/day in the limited condition; actual self-reported checking averaged roughly five versus about thirteen in the unlimited condition and about fifteen at baseline. Daily stress was lower during limited checking. The authors explicitly note that broader wellbeing/productivity links were indirect and correlational, that many outcomes were explored, that checking frequency was self-reported, and that there was no passive measurement-only control condition.

candidates.title: The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: a meta-analytic review of the testing effect
candidates.review_notes: The author-shared full article was reviewed, including the scope definition, inclusion logic, primary random-effects analysis, moderator analyses and discussion. The primary testing-versus-restudy estimate was positive (Hedges' g=0.50, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.58), but between-study heterogeneity was very high (I-squared=84.35). The effect varied with design and testing conditions; recall-based initial tests generally produced larger benefits than recognition tests, longer retention intervals were associated with larger effects, and feedback was associated with larger effects. The meta-analysis intentionally focused on testing versus an equivalent-duration restudy control rather than treating every retrieval-practice design as one interchangeable intervention.

candidates.title: Is Efficiency Overrated?: Minimal Social Interactions Lead to Belonging and Positive Affect
candidates.review_notes: Complete author-uploaded article reviewed alongside the journal record. Sixty people approaching a busy urban Starbucks were randomly assigned to make the barista interaction social or efficient. A research assistant blind to condition collected post-interaction measures. The social condition involved smiling, eye contact and brief conversation and produced higher positive affect, lower negative affect, greater satisfaction and greater belonging. The authors explicitly note that effects may be limited to contexts where service providers are willing and able to engage and may not generalize to pressured contexts. Outcomes were immediate and self-reported; the experiment does not establish durable social connection or treatment effects.

candidates.title: Effects of Empathic Paraphrasing – Extrinsic Emotion Regulation in Social Conflict
candidates.review_notes: The full article was reviewed, including intervention delivery, repeated-measures comparison, self-report and physiological results, discussion and limitations. The interviewer summarized facts, feelings and what mattered to the speaker, then asked whether the summary was accurate. The study supports only an immediate emotional-valence finding in a very small, trained-interviewer social-conflict setting; it did not measure comprehension accuracy, conflict resolution, relationship outcomes or ordinary listener training.

candidates.title: Consider it done! Plan making can eliminate the cognitive effects of unfulfilled goals
candidates.container_title: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
candidates.review_notes: Specific plan making reduced cognitive interference associated with unfinished goals in the reported experiments. This is convergent support for offloading an unfinished task into a concrete resumption plan, not evidence for a particular app or template.

candidates.title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis
candidates.review_notes: The complete public manuscript was reviewed, including terminology, inclusion criteria, coding, massed-versus-spaced comparisons, inter-study-interval and retention-interval analyses, fixed-versus-expanding comparisons, educational implications and limitations. The synthesis is directly relevant to repeated study of verbal material measured by later recall. It does not validate Brali's inherited daily AI schedule, retrieval-success thresholds, neuroscience explanation, habit tracking or transfer to complex skills.

candidates.title: Considering the opposite: A corrective strategy for social judgment
candidates.container_title: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
candidates.review_notes: Complete article reviewed through an available full-text copy and checked against the PubMed/APA record. Across two experiments totaling 150 undergraduates, consider-the-opposite instructions or materials reduced biased assimilation and biased hypothesis testing more than generic instructions to be fair and unbiased. The authors also note circumstances where considering the opposite could itself overweight disconfirming information. The experiments are classic task-specific social-judgment evidence, not proof of durable or domain-general debiasing.

candidates.review_notes: Very fresh peer-reviewed lead published 31 August 2026. The primary publisher abstract reports a 12-week randomized behavioral trial at two universities (397 enrolled; 224 completers) comparing a bundled Goal-Setting intervention (expense tracking, explicit savings targets, progress feedback), a habit-substitution intervention, and control using objective bank-transaction data. Goal-setting reduced monetary consumption and improved account balances relative to control, while the habit arm did not show significant effects. The complete article body could not be reliably retrieved in this run, so this record remains screening and must not be used as reviewed evidence or to justify a public protocol yet.
